line.text: That is {name}, Chancellor: a manifesto red line, and the words are on the record. Nothing here will stop you. On Budget day the public’s rating starts at the floor, whatever else you do.
line.short: {name} is a manifesto red line, Chancellor. The public’s rating starts at the floor.

line.text: {name} is tested, not broken: a tax rise in all but name. The words are kept, and the benches and the public will still notice.
line.short: {name} is tested, not broken: a tax rise in all but name.

line.text: On these numbers a rule is missed, and the OBR will say so on 28 October. The Charter’s escape clause is for an emergency or a significant shock, judged by the OBR, not for a choice.
line.short: On these numbers a rule is missed, and the OBR will say so.

line.text: {name} is a priority you agreed with the Prime Minister. Nothing in your Budget delivers it yet.
line.short: {name} is an agreed priority. Nothing in your Budget delivers it yet.

line.text: {name} is only partly delivered: an option has been adjusted on the desk below what it needs.
line.short: {name} is only partly delivered: an option was adjusted below what it needs.

line.text: Every priority you agreed with the Prime Minister has something behind it. What remains is whether the rules and your headroom survive the October forecast.
line.short: Every priority has something behind it; now the rules and headroom must survive October.

line.text: Headroom is below the target you set yourself. Remember what it is: a forecast margin. The OBR’s typical five-year error on receipts alone is about £32bn, bigger than any target on that list.
line.short: Headroom is below the target you set yourself, and it is a forecast margin.

line.text: You are inside your own target. It is still a forecast: the OBR’s typical error over five years is about £32bn, and October’s numbers will be the OBR’s, not ours.
line.short: Inside your own target, and still a forecast: October’s numbers will be the OBR’s.
